parties:
Kashem Ali
Vs.
The state & ors.
full_judgment: 13. Mr. Fazlul Karim, learned advocate for the appellant, argued before us that the statements of the deceased were arbitrarily discarded on the ground that they were not corroborated by independent witnesses and circumstances and probabilities. Upon exam mining the evidence on record it seems there were other substantial grounds to doubt the alleged statements of the deceased. As far as Ext.2 the alleged dying declaration recorded by the doctor is concerned, the same clearly deserves to be ignored because admittedly it was not a voluntary statement of the deceased but was made in response to questions put by the doctor and the questions were not admittedly recorded by the doctor. The Additional Sessions Judge has noticed if those questions were leading questions Ext.2 could not be accepted as genuine. Secondly the High Court Division noticed that there was interpolation in the statement by different pen. On top of all this there was a big question as to whether the deceased was physically in a position to make such lengthy statements at Islampur Thana Despensary where his condition was found to be grave. P.W.13, the doctor who examined him at about 9 p.m. (Exts.2 and 3 were allegedly recorded at the same time, 9 p.m.) stated that all the injuries (15) were profusely bleeding and fresh, Condi-tion of the injured was very grave and O.C. Islampur P.S. was duly informed. It is difficult to understand how the doctor and the Police-Officer could record such lengthy statements at the same time. The O.C. said in his evidence that he learnt from the doctor that the condition of Shamser Ali Amin was bad and that he might sink at any time.
